data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Wart & antiviral agents_

**Class:** Vesicant terpenoid (from blister beetle, Cantharis vesicatoria)

## Mechanism of action
- Activates neutral serine proteases → breaks desmosomal plaques → intraepidermal acantholysis → blister lifts off the lesion; painless at application

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Molluscum contagiosum (0.7% topical solution approved in USA 2023 for age ≥2 years)
- Common and periungual warts (with podophyllin and salicylic acid in some formulations)

## Dose & formulations
- Apply a small drop to each lesion in clinic; wash off after 4–6 h (molluscum: 24 h per label for the approved product); repeat every 3 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Blistering (expected), pain, burning, ring warts (annular recurrence), scarring, pigment change; toxic if ingested

## Contraindications
- Face, genitals, mucosa; diabetes/peripheral vascular disease (feet)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- Painless at application, blister in 24 h
- Ring warts after treatment
- Now approved for molluscum

_Sources: Khopkar ch.20 (Cantharidin); Wolverton 4e ch.43. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
